incorporated_articles.title: Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI

units.text: AI stakeholders should view this document as an addendum to the Software Code of Practice. We believe a Code focused specifically on the cyber security of AI is needed because AI has distinct differences to software. These include security risks from data poisoning, model obfuscation, indirect prompt injection and operational differences associated with data management.
units.text_start: an addendum to the Software Code of Practice

units.text: Shall Indicates a requirement for the voluntary Code. Should Indicates a recommendation for the voluntary Code.
units.text_start: Indicates a requirement for the voluntary Code
units.text_end: Indicates a recommendation for the voluntary Code

units.section: Principle 1: Raise awareness of AI security threats and risks
units.text: Organisations’ cyber security training programme shall include AI security content which shall be regularly reviewed and updated. AI security training shall be tailored to the specific roles and responsibilities of staff members.
units.text_start: cyber security training programme shall include AI security content
units.text_end: tailored to the specific roles and responsibilities of staff members

units.section: Principle 2: Design your AI system for security as well as functionality and performance
units.text: As part of deciding whether to create an AI system, a System Operator and/or Developer shall conduct a thorough assessment that includes determining and documenting the business requirements and/or problem they are seeking to address, along with associated AI security risks and mitigation strategies.
units.text_start: shall conduct a thorough assessment that includes determining and documenting the business requirements
units.text_end: associated AI security risks and mitigation strategies

units.text: Developers and System Operators shall ensure that AI systems are designed and implemented to withstand adversarial AI attacks, unexpected inputs and AI system failure.
units.text_end: unexpected inputs and AI system failure

units.section: Principle 4: Enable human responsibility for AI systems
units.text: When designing an AI system, Developers and/or System Operators should incorporate and maintain capabilities to enable human oversight.

units.section: Principle 5: Identify, track and protect your assets
units.text: Developers, Data Custodians and System Operators shall maintain a comprehensive inventory of their assets (including their interdependencies/connectivity).
units.text_start: shall maintain a comprehensive inventory of their assets

units.text: Developers and System Operators shall follow secure software supply chain processes for their AI model and system development.
units.text_start: shall follow secure software supply chain processes

units.text: System Operators that choose to use or adapt any models, or components, which are not well-documented or secured shall be able to justify their decision to use such models or components through documentation.
units.text_start: not well-documented or secured shall be able to justify their decision

units.section: Principle 8: Document your data, models and prompts
units.text: Developers shall document and maintain a clear audit trail of their system design and post-deployment maintenance plans.
units.text_start: shall document and maintain a clear audit trail

units.section: Principle 9: Conduct appropriate testing and evaluation
units.text: Developers shall ensure that all models, applications and systems that are released to System Operators and/or End-users have been tested as part of a security assessment process.
units.text_start: have been tested as part of a security assessment process

units.text: System Operators shall convey to End-users in an accessible way where and how their data will be used, accessed and stored (for example, if it is used for model retraining, or reviewed by employees or partners).
units.text_start: where and how their data will be used, accessed and stored

units.text: System Operators shall log system and user actions to support security compliance, incident investigations, and vulnerability remediation. System Operators should analyse their logs to ensure that AI models continue to produce desired outputs and to detect anomalies, security breaches, or unexpected behaviour over time.
units.text_start: shall log system and user actions

units.section: Principle 13: Ensure proper data and model disposal
units.text: If a Developer or System Operators decides to decommission a model and/or system, they shall involve Data Custodians and securely delete applicable data and configuration details.
units.text_start: shall involve Data Custodians and securely delete
